title: Power Automate Templates: 6 Worth Using in 2026
summary: Power Automate templates are pre-built workflows for routine tasks. This guide covers six options, from approvals to data sync, with setup instructions.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces does about this


The problem this article keeps returning to is that a template is only as usable as its weakest connector. You copy it, import it, and find out at switch-on that one step needs a licence you don't hold.


Activepieces handles that differently at the point where the check happens. Its core is MIT-licensed and you can self-host it, so the connector list does not depend on which plan a seat sits under.


A flow that calls an HTTP endpoint or a third-party app is the same kind of step as any other, and it doesn't push the whole flow into a higher tier the way Salesforce does in pick 6.


The catalogue is open, and you can count it. The MIT-licensed core carries 740 integrations, counted straight from the open-source monorepo on GitHub, and roughly 60% of them were contributed by the community. That matters for the job-first method the article argues for.


If the app your flow needs isn't there, you are not waiting on a vendor's priorities.


You can generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, or read the code of one that exists and see what it actually does before you build on it.


None of this makes the Microsoft-centred picks here worth moving. The approval, SharePoint filing and Teams digest flows sit on standard connectors and cost nothing beyond the seat you already pay for, so keep them in Power Automate.


Activepieces earns its place when the job runs across Slack, Google Workspace, a database or a CRM, or when you would otherwise be pricing ten Premium seats at $150 a month for one alert.


Pick the template by the job and by connector tier first, as the article says, and if the tier check sends you to a bill you don't want,[start the same flow free in Activepieces](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fpower-automate-templates-6-worth-using-in-2026) .
